qa_pairs.question: What types of advanced computing services are available for researchers to access through the Resource Allocation Competition (RAC)?
qa_pairs.answer: Through the Resource Allocation Competition (RAC), researchers can request access to a broad spectrum of advanced computing services, including general-purpose systems, large shared memory systems, general-purpose computing on graphics processing units, storage, and cloud resources.

qa_pairs.question: What kind of technical support can researchers expect with an allocation from the Resource Allocation Competition (RAC)?
qa_pairs.answer: With an allocation, researchers can receive technical support from a team of experts. This assistance includes installing and configuring software packages, help with code optimization, and detailed advice on solving technical issues. However, this support is generally limited to problems requiring a few days of effort, not deep or embedded programming support over several months.

qa_pairs.question: Should applicants consult with technical staff before submitting their Resource Allocation Competition (RAC) application?
qa_pairs.answer: Yes, it is strongly recommended that all applicants consult with technical staff responsible for the clusters they intend to use before submitting their Resource Allocation Competition (RAC) application. This ensures the technical aspects of the proposals align well with the requested clusters. PIs who have not previously used the clusters are especially advised to discuss their proposal with staff in advance to allow time for any necessary revisions. For guidance on whom to contact, applicants can email allocations@tech.alliancecan.ca.
